merger_name: MA Financial (Redcape Fund) – Seven hospitality venues in NSW

targets.name: Sydney Junction Hotel Property Pty Ltd

events.title: Notification waiver determination published
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Redcape Hotel Group Pty Ltd and MAHF Custodian Pty Ltd as
custodian for RGM TT PTY LTD (which is the trustee for each sub-
trust that will hold the respective target venues) (together, the
Acquirers) applied for a notification waiver in respect of their
proposed acquisition of 100% of the freehold land interest, buildings,
licenses, and other business assets of 7 hospitality venues in the
Hunter region of New South Wales (NSW), as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).
The 7 hospitality venues comprise of:
a. Gunyah Hotel, Belmont;
b. Argenton Hotel, Argenton;
c. Peden’s Hotel, Cessnock;
d. Sydney Junction Hotel, Hamilton;
e. Hotel Elermore, Elermore Vale;
f. Edgeworth Tavern, Edgeworth; and
g. QT Newcastle, Newcastle (target venues).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The Acquirers are part of MA Financial Group’s Redcape Fund, which
owns and operates community pubs and hotels. It currently has 37
pubs and hotels across NSW, Queensland, and Victoria.
The target venues are owned by entities controlled by Iris Capital.
With the exception of QT Newcastle, each target venue is a
community pub and hotel venue that offers food, beverage, gaming,
entertainment, and/or function and event services. QT Newcastle is
a tourist focused accommodation hotel that also offers food,
beverage, gaming, entertainment, and function and event services.
Five of the target venues offer accommodation, and the remaining
two (Hotel Elermore and Edgeworth Tavern) each operate an
associated ‘Bottler’ retail liquor store. Two target venues also have
an adjoining residential lot.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given there is no horizontal overlap between MA
Financial Group (or its connected entities) and the target venues in
the supply of on-premises liquor, dining, and gaming services, or the
retail supply of takeaway packaged liquor, in the Hunter region.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
